title: Redwood + Constellation joint solution technical sync
topics: Joint solution billing and support model
summary: Sync to align on marketplace listing checklist, network and security reference architecture for Constellation private deployments, and joint solution packaging. Action items include sharing reference diagrams, procurement contact, and a small benchmark plan for latency/cost targets. Some minor transcript noise; discussed possibility of a pilot on Redwood Dedicated and marketplace listing timeline.
action_items: Diego Ramos: share reference architecture diagram (VPC, peering, KMS flow) by 2026-03-24
Maya Singh: send Constellation marketplace onboarding doc and contract point-of-contact by 2026-03-22
Lena Park: provide draft marketplace listing copy and pricing ranges by 2026-03-26
Arjun Patel: run lightweight latency benchmark (10k tokens/simulated) and share results by 2026-04-02
next_steps: Schedule follow-up demo for Dedicated deployment (team + infra) week of 2026-03-30
Exchange security questionnaire and SOC2 artifacts via secure link
Confirm pilot scope and success metrics (latency <120ms p95, cost target per 1k tokens)
transcript: [00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — I'm Lena from Redwood, Diego's here from solutions, and Priya is on for product. How's everyone?
[00:08] Maya Singh: Hi Lena, thanks. Maya here. Ben and Arjun are also on. Sorry, we're in different time zones so thanks for working with us.
[00:15] Ben Ortiz: Hey all, excited to sync. We got the initial partner NDA signed so we can talk shop.
[00:25] Diego Ramos: Awesome. Agenda — marketplace listing steps, reference arch for private deployments (VPC, peering, KMS), and joint solution ops/support model. Any additions?
[00:32] Arjun Patel: Maybe also talk pilot metrics and the billing flow when listed in Constellation marketplace.

[00:40] Lena Park: Perfect, we'll cover billing and the billing integration patterns — direct billing vs. marketplace metered billing. Quick note, I'll say Redwood Dedicated sometimes shows up as 'Redwod Dedicate' in early docs, oops, but official name is Redwood Dedicated.
[00:58] Maya Singh: (laughs) we've seen that. On our side marketplace team wants the listing by end of April for the May release cycle.

[01:10] Diego Ramos: Good, timeline's workable. On the reference arch: for private deployments we have two common patterns — VPC peering into Redwood Private control plane with customer-managed egress, or an on-prem bundle for air-gapped. For Constellation I think VPC peering + KMS integration makes sense.
[01:34] Arjun Patel: Can you clarify the KMS path? We need to know if keys stay in our HSM and whether Redwood can do envelope encryption or if we push model artifacts to our side.

[01:46] Diego Ramos: Yes — we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM via KMIP). Typical flow is: customer keys encrypt data at rest; Redwood control plane stores encrypted object; runtime in your VPC gets access via a customer-maintained IAM role. But I'll share a diagram — apologies if I say KV cache wrong sometimes, it's KV cache not K-V cash, ha.
[02:05] Maya Singh: (background) that's helpful. For compliance we need audit logs with per-request tokens and key rotation notes. Do you produce audit logs that we can ingest into our SIEM?

[02:15] Priya Nair: Yes — we emit audit logs and can forward via secure syslog/S3 delivery. Logs include model/version, request id, token usage, and user id when available. There's also an option for long-term retention as an add-on. We'll share the retention matrix.
[02:31] Ben Ortiz: Great, marketplace listing — what do you need from us?

[02:36] Lena Park: We need listing copy (we can draft), logos, an integration checklist (which includes network, security, billing), and a joint solution one-pager. Also we need contact for procurement so Redwood legal can align on the reseller terms if Constellation wants to be a reseller.

[02:50] Ben Ortiz: I'll be the head contact for marketplace commercial, Ben Ortiz. I'll drop Maya the procurement person on the thread too. There's also a standard Constellation marketplace security questionnaire — we'll send that after the call.
[03:03] Diego Ramos: On the pilot — recommended scope: 2 nodes on Redwood Dedicated for 2 weeks with traffic replay, we can measure p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens. Is that feasible for you?
[03:12] Arjun Patel: Yes that seems reasonable. We prefer not to put customer data in hosted environment; we can replay sanitized logs into a private VPC test setup.
[03:20] Maya Singh: One question on network topology — do we need a NAT or can we do private link? We prefer PrivateLink for egress control.
[03:27] Diego Ramos: We support PrivateLink and VPC peering; PrivateLink is often recommended for tighter network boundaries. Will note that in the reference arch.

[03:40] Lena Park: On billing integration: Constellation marketplace supports metered usage and reseller margins. Two options: 1) direct billing via Redwood and provide partner referral fee, 2) marketplace metered billing where Constellation handles customer billing and buys from Redwood via reseller contract. We'll draft both flows for clarity.
[03:58] Ben Ortiz: For go-to-market we'd want the marketplace listing to link to a joint deployment guide and a demo video. Can Redwood produce a short 3–5 minute demo?
[04:06] Priya Nair: Yes we can produce a short demo clip and a one-page deployment guide. We'll coordinate on the script. Diego will own the reference arch diagram.
[04:15] Arjun Patel: Regarding security — SSO is a must, we use SAML 2.0 and Okta. How's SAML mapping and RBAC handled?

[04:23] Diego Ramos: We support SAML/Okta and SCIM provisioning for user sync. Roles can be mapped to Redwood RBAC at the org/team level. There's sometimes a small mismatch with resource tags but it's usually solvable via attribute mapping.
[04:38] Maya Singh: Good. Also need to validate SOC2 artifacts and pen test summary. Where do we get those?

[04:44] Lena Park: We'll share a secure link to our compliance bundle (SOC2 report, pen test summary redacted) — I'll put that in next steps. Some customers want an IP allowlist for control plane access; we can provide ASN/IP ranges.
[04:57] Ben Ortiz: Minor question — how do you handle model variants in the marketplace listing? If a customer wants quantized smaller models vs. full-sized models, can we show options?

[05:05] Priya Nair: Absolutely — the listing can show available model variants, recommended latency and cost profiles, and a suggested default for the joint solution. We'll include performance profiles per model.
[05:18] Arjun Patel: About deployments — you mentioned on-prem bundle for air-gapped. Is that a supported GA path?

[05:24] Diego Ramos: Yes, on-prem bundle is available for enterprise customers; it requires a longer validation and a signed private deployment agreement. For Constellation's use case VPC-based private deployment looks faster.
[05:37] Maya Singh: Can you also support token-level cost reporting so we can show customers estimated per-call cost in the marketplace UI?
[05:44] Lena Park: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token breakdown and per-route cost estimates. We can provide a small JSON feed or an embed for marketplace if needed.
[05:55] Ben Ortiz: (typing) we'll want that JSON schema please.

[06:00] Diego Ramos: I'll attach the schema and an example in the follow-up email. Note: sometimes the auto-transcript thinks 'KV cache' is 'K V cash' — forgive typos in the transcript, you'll see that in the notes.
[06:12] Maya Singh: No worries. A couple of edge questions: SLA expectations, and will Redwood provide L2 support during the pilot?
[06:20] Priya Nair: For pilots we provide L2 support; for production we have SLA-backed offerings on Dedicated and Private with escalation. We'll outline support SLAs in the partner onboarding doc.
[06:33] Arjun Patel: For the benchmark — what traffic shape do you need? We were thinking bursty real-world traffic with inference sequences up to 512 tokens.

[06:42] Diego Ramos: 512 tokens is fine. For realistic cost/latency numbers we'll want a mix: 70% short queries (<=64 tokens) and 30% long (256–512). We'll share a small harness script to replay traffic.
[06:56] Ben Ortiz: On commercialization, do you have suggested partner discount tiers?
[07:01] Lena Park: We'll propose partner tiers in the draft — typical structure is referral fee + volume discounts for committed capacity on Dedicated.
[07:10] Maya Singh: Any blockers we foresee for Constellation marketplace listing?
[07:14] Diego Ramos: Main blockers: compliance artifacts and integration checklist completion. We'll work to reduce friction by pre-populating the listing fields and offering a quick start template.
[07:25] Ben Ortiz: Sounds good. Let's run through that checklist quickly so we can close open items today if possible.

[07:31] Lena Park: Checklist items — logos and listing copy (Ben), contact for procurement (Ben/Maya), security questionnaire (Constellation sends), reference arch diagram (Diego), demo video (Redwood), pilot scope and dates (both teams). Any other?
[07:45] Arjun Patel: We'll also need the support contact and who will be on-call during pilot (we can provide ours).
[07:50] Priya Nair: Noted. We'll include Redwood on-call details in the partner packet.
[07:58] Maya Singh: Ok, timeline recap? We want listing by end of April so can you confirm deliverables dates?

[08:05] Lena Park: Sure — Diego diagram by 3/24, Maya/procurement contact by 3/22, Lena listing draft by 3/26, pilot bench results by 4/02. We can target a follow-up week of 3/30 for demo and pilot kickoff.
[08:20] Ben Ortiz: Works for me. I'll open a Constellation ticket with the marketplace ops team after this call.

[08:27] Diego Ramos: One more technical note — we have network egress and model registry considerations. If you want to host model artifacts inside Constellation's object storage, that's supported; otherwise Redwood can host model bits encrypted with your KMS.
[08:43] Arjun Patel: Prefer models inside our storage for full control, but need to understand the latency impact. Will the runtime fetch models at startup only?
[08:52] Diego Ramos: Yes, we cache model artifacts locally in the runtime; initial pull is paid in setup time but not on per-request. We'll document the cold-start behavior in the ref arch.
[09:03] Maya Singh: Cool. Anything else?
[09:06] Lena Park: Quick ask — can Constellation share a short use case blurb we can put on the listing? A sentence or two. Ben?
[09:12] Ben Ortiz: Yes, we'll provide a blurb. I'll coordinate with Maya and product marketing and share by 3/26.
[09:18] Priya Nair: Perfect. I'll call out the action items in the follow-up email and attach the draft listing and security bundle link.
[09:24] Maya Singh: Thank you. Look forward to the diagrams. I'll send the security questionnaire after we drop off the recording in our ticket.
[09:32] Lena Park: Great. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the attachments and schedule the demo. Talk soon.
[09:37] (call ends)
